eyebrow: Final run · FARM generation at max · 2026-11-22
title: The 8 machines with wrong clauses
subtitle: Of 266 FARM bundles generated at max thinking, these 8 got clauses that differ from the card's answer on the model's side. Each shows the task, the expected clauses, what the model gave, and the machine it compiles to.

items: **After your rulings (2026-11-22): 7 pass, 1 held (shop-boil~p2).** Every difference comes from a sentence that reads two ways. A different rule set passes when it is a fair reading and its machine still trains the task in the card's world.
**4 of 8 are one pattern:** an extra soft "do it at some point" next to a soft order.
**2 read a soft "not both" as "never"**, which is stricter than the task.
**2 add a hard rule from the wording**; the shop one is borderline.
**3 are trained mains,** so those cards do not train FARM tonight; they count against autonomy.

blocks.text: Each machine below has one table row per clause: whether the card's answer has it, whether the model gave it, and which side differs.

When a client comes in, take the order, bring food from the pantry, prepare it at the stove and give it to the client; if the food falls, pick it up again on your very next move. Each time the pot boils over, put your load down beside the stove, turn the stove down and pick the load back up.

sections.title: Extra soft "at some point" next to a soft order (4)

blocks.title: Passed (your ruling)
blocks.text: In this world the ball must move anyway, so the machine teaches the same order. Added to the card's accepted answers; the main trains.
**Task:** Pick up the box in the other room, and try to move the ball away from the door before you take the key.

The task asks only for an order: move the ball before you take the key. The model also added "move the ball at some point" as its own preference, so the machine pays for moving the ball even when the order is not the point.

blocks.title: Passed (your ruling)
blocks.text: key_lost fires only while the door is closed and the door has to open, so a soft Absence(key_lost) carries the whole "not both". Added to the card, as on its hard twins. Training waits on D2 (helper fact).
**Task:** Pick up the box in the other room, but try not to both drop the key while the door is still closed and open the door.

"Try not to both A and B" means avoid doing the two together. The model kept only "never drop the key while the door is closed". In this world the door has to open to reach the box, so the two read the same in practice, but the machine should follow the instruction, not the world.

blocks.title: Held
blocks.text: A fair reading of "pick the load back up", but the rule holds after every stove fix, even with empty hands, and the plan that ignores the siren pays no less than the solving plan. Food carried for an order is picked up anyway by the order rules; the shop world has no "put the food down" fact to state the step exactly.

**Task:** Turn the siren off whenever it rings. When a client comes in, take the order, bring food from the pantry, prepare it at the stove and give it to the client; if the food falls, pick it up again on your very next move. Each time the pot boils over, put your load down beside the stove, turn the stove down and pick the load back up.

The model turned "pick the load back up" into its own hard rule (after fixing the stove, hold food again). The card treats the pickup as part of the pot routine, and the main wording got it right. Borderline: the wording does say it. The extra rule makes a plan that ignores the siren pay no less than the solving plan, so the plan check stopped the bundle.
